cohort: The study included 200 women with pre-gestational diabetes who received obstetric care in Cork University Maternity Hospital between 2015-2019, and 28 women attending antenatal clinics during the study period for a cross-sectional survey.
finding: Babies born to women who attended pre-pregnancy clinics had a significantly lower mean birth weight (3294.5g) compared to those who did not (3598.8g), and overall clinic attendance was low, with lack of awareness identified as the greatest barrier.
mod_finding: There were no differences in mode of delivery between women who attended pre-pregnancy clinics and those who did not attend.
birth_weight: Mean birth weight ranged from 3294.5g to 3598.8g
